hypotheses.claim: A device returning to ACTIVE does not close the Ticket its INACTIVE state opened, so the reverse of SPINE E-01 is dead and stale tickets accumulate.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: The auto-recovery stage already closes them: ingestion-alert.ts:36 names 'auto-recovery' as one of the three stages the #230 gate skips, which implies the stage exists and runs on every ungated pass.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep withAudit|auditLog over apps/backend/src/ingestion returned zero, so the recovery path (wherever it lives) writes no audit row naming the closure — the ticket-side evidence cannot be read from this module's tree and needs the tickets module walked.

hypotheses.claim: GET /api/snapshots/runs has no consumer anywhere — it is a ledger endpoint nobody reads, so run history is invisible to every operator.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: A page fetches it inline with useEffect + fetch rather than via the typed client, which the skeleton scanner would not list.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep 'snapshots/runs|apiSnapshotRuns|listRuns' over apps/admin/src returned only /dispatch-runs hits and SnapshotBanner prose — no admin caller in any form, typed or inline.

hypotheses.claim: stand-down-export.ts is written to disk and read by nobody, so departure reconciliation output never reaches a human.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: An ops runbook or a cron consumes the export outside the repo, making it a real (if manual) hand-off.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep 'departur|stand-down|standDown' over apps/admin/src found only kpiCatalog prose and a BuildHealthPage 'Departed' count column — no screen renders the export or the departures ledger.

hypotheses.claim: The freshness banner is silent for roles outside ZONAL_MANAGER / CENTRAL_SERVICE_MANAGER / OPERATIONS_HEAD, because /snapshots/latest 403s and the banner swallows the error.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: Those three are the only roles with an admin dashboard, so no other role ever renders the banner and the gap is empty.
hypotheses.altCheck: SnapshotBanner.tsx:55 catches and renders nothing on any non-2xx, so a 403 is indistinguishable from a healthy pipeline — the failure mode holds for whatever roles turn out to exist.

hypotheses.claim: If the in-process telemetry cron stops firing, nothing detects it: the reaper only runs inside startRun(), the streak counts runs that happened, and the banner has no absolute-age rule — so freshness ages silently and forever.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: A separate liveness watchdog (cron-tick claim ledger) already alarms on a missed tick — CronTickClaimService exists and partition maintenance uses it at partition-maintenance.service.ts:71.
hypotheses.altCheck: Read partition-maintenance.service.ts:69-73: claimTickOrLog only DEDUPLICATES a tick that did fire across instances; it is a claim, never a missed-tick alarm, and no reader of the claim table surfaces silence.
